stories.title: Sweetener used in chewing gum and jam linked to strokes and heart attacks
stories.summary: High blood levels of xylitol associated with higher risk of major cardiovascular events, in largest study of its kind A common sweetener used in products such as chewing gum, toothpaste, jam, yoghurts and ice-cream has been linked to an increased risk of strokes, heart attacks and death. Xylitol is a sugar alcohol present in some natural foods in very low amounts. It is also added – often in amounts 1,000 times higher – to artificially sweeten foods, beverages and oral care products. stories.title: Vietnam demands end to activity in Paracels after report of Chinese construction
stories.summary: HANOI, Aug 28 - Vietnam said on Friday it strongly opposed all foreign activities in the Paracels archipelago in the disputed South China Sea, following a report earlier this week of new Chinese construction on an islet there.
article_sentences: Vietnam said on Friday it strongly opposed all foreign activities in the Paracels archipelago in the disputed South China Sea, following a report earlier this week of new Chinese construction on an islet there.

Reuters reported on Tuesday that new installations had been sighted on Yagong Island, called Ba Island by Vietnam, citing satellite imagery, with security analysts saying it could be the start of an early-warning radar facility.

"Vietnam resolutely opposes this, has made serious representations and affirmed its position on the matter, and demands an immediate end to such activities and that they not be repeated," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Pham Thu Hang told Reuters in an emailed statement.
China has occupied the Paracel Islands since 1974, when it seized them from the navy of the former South Vietnam.
Vietnam, which claims the entire grouping as its own, has moved in recent years to expand its own network of bases in the Spratlys, which lie further south.
The Spratlys and nearby waters are also claimed, fully or in part, by Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, Taiwan and Brunei.
Hang said Vietnam has sufficient historical evidence and legal grounds to affirm its sovereignty over the Paracels in accordance with international law.

"Vietnam reiterates that all foreign activities in the Paracel Islands, including at Ba Island and at Hai Sam Reef, conducted without Vietnam's permission are completely illegal and null and void," she said, using Vietnam's name for Antelope Reef.

stories.title: Singapore, Uzbekistan take first step towards free trade agreement
stories.summary: The proposed agreement aims to improve market access and create more opportunities for businesses in both countries.
article_sentences: Singapore and Uzbekistan have taken the first formal step towards negotiating a free trade agreement (FTA), as the two countries seek to deepen economic ties and expand the opportunities for businesses.

The two countries signed a joint statement on Aug 28 formalising their intention to begin negotiations on a bilateral FTA, during Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong’s official visit to the Central Asian nation.

Lee and Uzbekistan’s Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade, Laziz Kudratov, witnessed the signing, along with two other agreements aimed at deepening economic cooperation between the two countries.

These were a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on cooperation in investment, industry, and trade, and a supplemental MOU for a planned investment between an Indorama-Wilmar joint venture and the government of Uzbekistan.

“This milestone represents a commitment to start talks for a bilateral FTA,” a Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) spokesman said, adding that the framework for negotiations towards a “modern and business-facilitative FTA” was now being built.
FTAs are agreements between countries that seek to reduce or remove barriers to trade, such as tariffs, and make it easier for businesses to access each other’s markets.
The proposed agreement aims to improve market access and create more opportunities for businesses in both countries.
It comes as economic links between Singapore and Uzbekistan have grown in recent years.
Uzbekistan was Singapore’s second-largest services trading partner in Central Asia in 2024 and its third-largest goods trading partner in the region in 2025.
Bilateral trade in goods amounted to $69 million in 2025, while trade in services stood at $109.6 million in 2024.
Singapore’s direct investment in Uzbekistan amounted to $390 million in 2024.
The other agreements signed on Aug 28 also seek to build on the growing economic links.
